core_obligations: Choose U over which s generates L (proof lines 6775-6778).
Show every relevant prime divisor is a component of X minus U (proof lines 6778-6780).
Apply local finiteness of components (proof lines 6780-6781).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a locally Noetherian integral X, an invertible module L and a regular meromorphic section s, both the set of prime divisors Z whose generic point satisfies s not in L_xi and the set of prime divisors with ord_{Z,L}(s) nonzero are locally finite in X (source lines 6758-6773). The proof finds a nonempty open U over which s corresponds to a section of L generating L, observes that any prime divisor occurring in either set must be an irreducible component of the complement of U, and invokes local finiteness of the components of a closed subset.
